title: QUIC Simulator-Backed Correctness Scenario Work Item
summary: Define and implement the first narrow simulator-backed scenario accounting surface that maps controlled network conditions to existing QUIC requirements, expected observables, evidence bundles, and promotion rules without changing runtime transport behavior.
planned_changes:
- Define the scenario registry model, initial scenario families, status vocabulary, and evidence rules.
- Classify each scenario as correctness, advisory-interop, or performance-only so advisory peer characterization and benchmark-style measurements do not become support claims by accident.
- Map each correctness scenario to existing RFC 9000, RFC 9002, CRT, or INT requirement IDs instead of creating parameter-only normative requirements.
- Allow advisory and performance-only scenarios to use `REQ-QUIC-INT-0026` as an accounting anchor only when their promotion rule says no protocol correctness claim is promoted.
- Define artifact roots for simulator evidence, including logs, qlog, pcaps, simulator stdout, runner report when applicable, deterministic seed or droplist material, upstream simulator source reference or pinned commit/path, and the exact simulator command/profile.
- Add `scripts/interop/Invoke-QuicNetworkSimulatorScenario.ps1` as the first manual helper for `SIM-QUIC-BASE-0001` and `SIM-QUIC-LOSS-0001` only.
- Add focused tests that prove plan-only output, deterministic droplist validation, and evidence-bundle writing without requiring the real upstream simulator checkout.
- Defer blackhole/PTO recovery, deterministic reordering, corruption discard, rebind characterization, cross-traffic measurement, generated scenario inventory output, and hosted workflow dispatch until the baseline and deterministic-loss evidence shape is stable.
completion_notes: Completed the first simulator-backed scenario accounting implementation slice without runtime transport changes. Added the manual helper for `SIM-QUIC-BASE-0001` and `SIM-QUIC-LOSS-0001`, preserved minimum evidence bundles under `artifacts/network-simulator/<scenario-id>/<run-id>/`, required explicit droplist material for deterministic-loss proof, matched the upstream docker-compose model, kept Docker launch behind explicit `-Execute`, preserved preflight and docker-compose failure evidence, and added focused requirement-home and helper tests. The helper-owned endpoint staging path prepares Incursa.Quic client/server Docker contexts, compose override, `/www`, `/downloads`, and `/certs` roots for baseline and deterministic-loss transfer evidence without changing runtime transport code; `/www` is mounted into both endpoint containers because the client-side transfer completion boundary checks the known source length. Focused validation passed: `pwsh -NoProfile -File scripts\Validate-SpecTraceJson.ps1 -Profiles core -JsonReportPath .artifacts\spec-trace-current-status-check-after-force-recreate.json` validated 562 artifacts, and `dotnet test tests\Incursa.Quic.Tests\Incursa.Quic.Tests.csproj -c Release --no-restore --filter "FullyQualifiedName~NetworkSimulatorScenarioScriptTests|FullyQualifiedName~REQ_QUIC_INT_0026"` passed 9/9. Local upstream-checkout evidence-only preflights also preserved baseline and droplist compose plans under `.artifacts/network-simulator-local/...` with `execute_requested=false`. A live baseline simple-p2p run passed under `.artifacts/network-simulator-live/SIM-QUIC-BASE-0001/current-baseline-clean-compose-20260519`, completing the managed transfer and downloading 10,250 bytes. Deterministic loss execution remains open for `SIM-QUIC-LOSS-0001`; this does not claim qlog/pcap proof, hosted workflow coverage, rebind/migration support, or broad simulator-matrix promotion.
out_of_scope: runtime-backed scenario expansion beyond SIM-QUIC-BASE-0001 and SIM-QUIC-LOSS-0001
making simulator runs blocking in ordinary CI
verification_plan: Review the scenario model, confirm the linked INT requirement and architecture artifact exist, confirm the first-wave scenario table maps correctness rows to existing requirement IDs, confirm advisory and performance-only rows cannot promote protocol correctness, and prove the first helper surface with focused `SIM-QUIC-BASE-0001` plus `SIM-QUIC-LOSS-0001` plan/evidence tests before expanding the matrix.
